title: Local lifting criterion for epic set-presheaf sheafification on a Grothendieck topology
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category and $J$ a Grothendieck topology: for each object $U$, $J(U)$ is a collection of sieves on $U$ containing the maximal sieve and satisfying pullback stability and transitivity. A sieve is a collection of arrows into $U$ closed under precomposition. Use set-valued presheaves in a universe containing the objects and arrows of $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $f:P\to Q$ be a morphism of such presheaves and let $f^\#:P^\#\to Q^\#$ be its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Then $f^\#$ is an epimorphism of sheaves (right cancellation holds against every pair of sheaf morphisms) if and only if, for every $U$ and $q\in Q(U)$, the sieve
$$\{u:V\to U\mid \text{there exists }p\in P(V)\text{ with }f_V(p)=Q(u)(q)\}$$
belongs to $J(U)$. Equivalently every section of $Q$ lifts through $f$ after restriction along a covering family, where a family covers when its generated sieve belongs to $J(U)$. No fibre products in $\mathcal C$ and no subcanonical hypothesis are required.
